Applied Intuition is looking for senior software engineers with passion and expertise in owning and maintaining HD maps infrastructure for autonomous vehicles.



At Applied we treat maps not as a static dataset, but as a single integrated, self-healing data flywheel powering Physical AI. Fleets of vehicles collect ground truth from multimodal sensors which feed ingestion pipelines, dynamic change detection algorithms, machine learning models, and real-time onboard localization and map fusion —closing the loop between field data collection and instantaneous autonomy stack updates.



In this full time role on the Maps team, you will solve challenges at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, continuous data pipelines, and spatial visualization. You’ll be involved in whole life cycle of HD maps from gathering and codifying map requirements, supporting map visualization and editing, enabling large scale simulations, and publishing maps to AV fleets across multiple vehicle types worldwide – from long-haul L4 commercial trucks to L2++ personal cars, to heavy mining rigs, and tactical defense platforms. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design and build infrastructure and tools to provide high definition (HD) map creation, ingestion, and lifecycle management for autonomous vehicle and robotics development across all of Applied’s products

 - Define and own the Dana for Physical AI map storage format to handle heterogeneous features and distributed map data focusing on UIs, data pipelines and storage, CRUD operations, and SDKs

 - Design and develop a highly-scalable, high-performance real-time geometric query system to support highly performant three-dimensional spatial queries for vehicle dynamics modeling and testing in autonomous robotic platforms

 - Support tooling to digitize road network geometry, semantic attributes, and related infrastructure from lidar point clouds, high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery, street-level imagery, and other geospatial inputs

 - Validate map changes against rigorous mapping specifications to ensure high accuracy, completeness, and consistency of map data thru algorithmic and other quality validation checks

 - Support, triage, troubleshoot, and root cause map-related simulation and onroad disengagement system failures by correlating simulation results, dynamics behavior, and autonomy stack outputs

 - Collaborate with engineers and customers to gather requirements, plan features, and create roadmaps

 - Advise customers on the effective use of simulation and mapping tools to evaluate autonomy performance, safety, and system robustness


REQUIREMENTS

 - BS in in Computer Science, Robotics, Applied Mathematics, or related engineering field

 - 2+ years of experience in HD mapping for autonomous vehicles building software components or sub systems that address real-world mapping and/or localization challenges

 - 3+ years experience in programming & systems including: C++, Python, Go, JavaScript, SQL, Linux, and Git

 - Engineering Practices: Scalable distributed systems, CI/CD workflows, version control, and cross-team collaboration using Jira and Git-based tooling

 - A strong working understanding of lane-level geometry at CM precision, routing, and HD (High-Definition) map structures used in autonomous driving


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with Kubernetes, AWS, GCP, and/or Azure

 - Experience with large-scale data processing using frameworks

 - Deep hands-on expertise in relevant algorithms or methods, 3D geometry or distributed systems

 - Deep understanding of sensors used for localization, state of the art industry solutions, and common approaches for production systems

 - Experience working with point cloud data, 3D visualization environments, or lidar-based annotation tools

 - Experience using browser-based map editors or web-based 3D tooling

 - Familiarity with feedback loops between mapping, perception, localization, and planning teams

 - Familiarity with log-based resimulation tooling and simulation-based map validation

 - Build Test Tooling & Glue Code: Develop Python and C++ scripts for data reduction, log analysis, system validation, and real-time subsystem verification.

 - System Cabling & Electronics: Fabricate custom wiring harnesses, perform precision soldering, and define system-level architecture using clear block diagrams.

 - Manage Communications & Networks: Configure IP routing, subnets, and local network interfaces between flight controllers, companion computers, radios, and ground control stations.

 - Experience: 5+ years of experience in robotics integration, flight test engineering, embedded systems, or autonomous vehicles (aerial background preferred).

 - Linux & Networking Mastery: Deep practical comfort with the Linux CLI, file management, system logging, local IP routing, subnets, and containerized deployments (Docker).

 - Hardware & Electronics Capability: Proven hands-on skills in wiring, custom cable assembly, bench soldering, and physical diagnostics using oscilloscopes and multimeters.

 - Scripting & Glue Code: Strong proficiency in Python, C++, or Shell scripting for automation, test suite creation, and processing flight data logs.

 - Protocols: Direct experience working with serial and vehicle bus protocols (UART, CAN, Ethernet, SPI, I2C).

 - Leadership: Ability to lead major integration efforts independently and act as the technical link between software, GNC, and hardware teams.

 - Bachelors degree in any field, or equivalent combination of education and work experience.

 - Active DoD Secret Security Clearance.

 - Deep experience with the MAVLink protocol and autopilot hardware (PX4, ArduPilot).

 - Background working with defense tech platforms or flight ranges.

The robotics team builds that platform and uses it to deliver robot autonomy on customer lines, training, evaluating, and deploying policies on real robots doing real industrial tasks. Everyone on the team works hands-on with hardware and sees their work reach customers.

As a Robot Learning Engineer, you will work on manipulation policies from task definition to a policy running reliably on a physical robot. You will train and fine-tune policies, understand why they fail, and make them dependable enough for customer use. Success is measured on the robot, not only on offline benchmarks.

We are open to candidates at different experience levels who meet the requirements. We value demonstrated work on real systems, including equivalent practical experience, over a particular degree or title.

 


AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Work on the full learning loop for manipulation tasks: task definition, demonstration collection, data curation, training, real-robot evaluation, and deployment.

 - Train and fine-tune manipulation policies, from large pretrained models such as vision-language-action models to compact task-specific policies, and choose the right approach for each task.

 - Develop repeatable recipes for industrial tasks such as pick-and-place, bimanual handling, and contact-rich assembly, adding force or tactile signals where they help.

 - Deploy policies on edge compute and validate observation processing, action interfaces, and control timing on the robot.

 - Turn failures and human interventions into better data, better models, and better evaluation.

 - Measure what customers care about, including success rate, cycle time, intervention rate, and the data and time needed to reach a target, and improve those numbers task after task.

 - Package recipes and models so the next task, and the next robot, starts from what was learned on the last one.

 


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - 1+ years of professional experience

 - A Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent

 - Trained or fine-tuned a learned manipulation policy and deployed and evaluated it on a physical robot.

 - Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with the ability to write maintainable training, evaluation, and deployment code.

 - Practical depth in imitation learning and at least one modern policy family, such as vision-language-action models, diffusion policies, or action-chunking transformers.

 - Working knowledge of robot kinematics, coordinate frames, camera calibration, and the interface between learned actions and low-level control.

 - The habit of diagnosing failures with controlled experiments across data, sensing, model, and execution.

 - Comfort taking on open-ended problems and communicating tradeoffs clearly to teammates at the robot.

 


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience with bimanual manipulation, force-controlled insertion, tactile sensing, or dexterous hands.

 - Experience with ROS 2, LeRobot, or simulators such as Isaac and MuJoCo.

 - Experience optimizing inference on NVIDIA Jetson or GPU edge systems, including model export, compilation, or quantization.

 - Experience with reinforcement learning post-training, learning from interventions, or transferring policies across robot platforms.

ABOUT EPISCI

EpiSci, an Applied Intuition company, develops next-generation tactical autonomy solutions for national security problems. EpiSci's autonomy software is technology agnostic, operationally informed, and tactically relevant, and has piloted swarms of uncrewed aerial systems and tactical fighter aircraft. Additional applications include crewed-uncrewed teaming for air dominance, cognitive sensors, networks for advanced communications systems, and battle management command and control for informed decision-making. EpiSci delivers speed, cost-efficiency, and scalability as the preferred partner for defense agencies and industry teams seeking mission-critical autonomy solutions.




ABOUT THE ROLE

This ISSO owns the day-to-day security posture of EpiSci's classified information systems, collateral and Special Access Program, across our Irvine and Poway facilities.

You will build and maintain authorization packages under the Risk Management Framework, with implementation guidance drawn from JSIG, DAAPM, ICD-503, CMMC, and the NIST 800 series. You will work directly with the ISSM to attain and maintain assessment and authorization from government authorizing officials, from initial requirements through operational deployment and continuous monitoring.

This is a hands-on seat. The work includes configuring, scanning, remediating, and standing up enclaves alongside the documentation. You can expect regular interaction with government security offices and authorizing officials, DCSA, and program security teams, and a continuous review cadence on eMASS and program packages.

Program access: This position requires Special Access Program access. Prior SAP experience is strongly preferred. Candidates with collateral-only experience and a strong track record under RMF will be considered and read on after hire.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Maintain accredited classified systems in an authorized operating state while meeting program delivery timelines

 - Author, update, and defend RMF artifacts: System Security Plans (SSP), Security Assessment Reports (SAR), POA&Ms, Risk Assessment Reports, Configuration Management Plans, Incident Response Plans, Continuous Monitoring Plans, and hardware and software baselines

 - Execute continuous monitoring: ACAS and Nessus vulnerability scanning, SCAP and STIG compliance checking, audit log review, and remediation tracking against CAT I, II, and III findings

 - Support the design, development, and implementation of procedures and systems for secure facilities, and ensure facility compliance with requirements for classified information system processing

 - Conduct risk and vulnerability assessments of planned and installed systems to identify vulnerabilities, threats, and protection needs, and recommend mitigations

 - Lead periodic self-inspections and support DoD Cybersecurity On-Site Inspections, DCSA assessments, and customer security reviews across both sites

 - Serve as first-line response for classified security incidents and spillage: detect, contain, preserve evidence, document, and escalate through the ISSM and program security chain

 - Administer and harden classified computing and network infrastructure, including standing up and configuring new enclaves

 - Manage user account provisioning, privileged access review, media control, and trusted download and data transfer procedures

 - Deliver security awareness and system-specific training to cleared users and system administrators

 - Maintain working knowledge of evolving policy, regulation, and compliance guidance affecting classified computing assets


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, or a minimum of 5 years of ISSO, ISSE, or cybersecurity policy and engineering experience in a classified environment

 - DoD 8570/8140 IAM Level I/IAT Level 2 (Security +) as a condition of employment

 - Demonstrated proficiency applying RMF and writing authorization packages, with working knowledge of ICD-503, JSIG, and the NIST 800 series (800-53, 800-37, 800-171)

 - Hands-on experience with security tooling: NESSUS and ACAS, DISA STIGs, STIG Viewer, SCAP Compliance Checker, and HBSS or ESS

 - Experience designing, building, and maintaining information system enclaves, including the underlying computing hardware and network architecture

 - Working knowledge of incident response, disaster recovery, forensic principles, continuous monitoring, and cybersecurity hygiene

 - Active DoD security clearance (SECRET minimum) and U.S. citizenship


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Prior SAP experience as an ISSO, ISSE, or system administrator under JSIG, with current or recent program briefings

 - TS/SCI with the ability to obtain program access

 - eMASS, Xacta, or equivalent package management experience as a package author

 - Experience with DCSA DAAPM and NISPOM-governed facilities, including Co-Use or multi-program environments

 - Prior ISSM designation, or readiness to be designated ISSM for a smaller program

 - Hands-on Linux (RHEL, Rocky, Ubuntu) and Windows Server administration in air-gapped and cross-domain environments

 - Familiarity with cross-domain solutions, COMSEC and TACLANE operations, or trusted download procedures

 - CMMC assessment or preparation experience on the CUI side

 - Experience supporting a rapid-prototyping or startup defense environment


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THE FIRST YEAR

 - 90 days: Fully briefed and read on. Baseline established, with a complete inventory of accredited systems across Irvine and Poway, current POA&M status understood, and scan and audit cadence running on schedule.

 - 6 months: Self-inspection program running cleanly at both sites, package gaps closed, and established as the point of contact for the ISSM, program security, and government assessors.

 - 12 months: New program systems accredited on the timeline the program requires.


TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS

Willing to travel for company business between Irvine, CA and Poway, CA, as well as to customer and government sites (approximately 15-20%).




SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

 - Must be a U.S. Citizen

 - Must hold an active DoD security clearance

 - Must be eligible for and willing to accept Special Access Program briefings

 - Position is 100% on-site. Classified work cannot be performed remotely.

For more information about U.S. security clearances: https://www.state.gov/securityclearances

ABOUT THE ROLE

As Hardware Systems Lead for our drone program, you will be the hands-on chief engineer for the hardware that carries our autonomy into the air.  - Lead integration of sensors (cameras, lidar, radar, GNSS/IMU), compute, power systems, communications, and flight controllers onto airframes

 - Own size, weight, and power (SWaP) tradeoffs, balancing performance, flight time, payload capacity, and cost

 - Define hardware requirements and reference architectures that scale across aircraft configurations

 - Plan and run environmental, durability, and flight testing, analyze failures and crashes, and drive root cause and design fixes

 - Be the technical authority and escalation point for hardware tradeoffs across mechanical, electrical, avionics, software, autonomy, and flight test

 - Lead hardware design reviews, set engineering standards, and mentor other engineers

 - Support flight test campaigns, demonstrations, and field operations

 - BS/MS in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, or a related field

 - 10+ years of hands-on hardware engineering experience on drones, UAS, or other aircraft

 - Strong command of the whole hardware system: airframe and structures, electrical architecture, power distribution, harness design, avionics, and how they interact

 - A track record of designing hardware to survive demanding environments, with real experience in vibration, shock, ingress protection, thermal management, and EMI/EMC

 - Hands-on experience in the lab and in the field: building prototypes, wiring and debugging systems, running flight tests, and diagnosing failures and crashes

 - Experience integrating sensors such as cameras, lidar, radar, and GNSS/IMU, along with compute and flight control hardware, onto airborne platforms

 - Experience with SWaP optimization and lightweight design, including composites and carbon fiber

 - Experience with reliability and qualification testing (environmental testing, HALT, flight-hour tracking)

 - Systems-level thinking and the ability to make architecture decisions and defend them

 - Experience designing for manufacturability and field serviceability

Nice to have:

 - Experience with fixed-wing, multirotor, or VTOL platforms

 - Familiarity with aerospace standards such as DO-160 or MIL-STD-810 and MIL-STD-461

 - Experience with propulsion, battery, or power system integration

Security Requirement: 

 - US Citizen or US Green Card holder

ABOUT SEOUL

Applied Intuition entered the Korean market in 2020. The team has rapidly grown over the past few years and established strategic relationships with major Korean automotive OEM customers. Based in Gangnam, the Seoul site consists of employees who previously come from LG, Ansys, Unity, and other renowned companies.


About the Role

Our defense customers are building fleets of unmanned aerial systems that have to fly, coordinate, and complete missions in the real world. We build the tools they use to develop that autonomy. Building those tools well, and knowing they hold up outside of simulation, requires engineers who have done this work themselves.

We are seeking a Software Engineer to join our Korea office to build Applied Intuition's multi-agent autonomy development tools. This on-site role focuses on the capabilities defense  customers rely on to design, train, and validate coordinated UAV behavior. You will collaborate frequently with our U.S. product engineering team, and work directly with Korean defense customers to translate their operational requirements into product capabilities.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, develop, and maintain core features of Applied Intuition’s autonomy development tools, with a focus on multi-agent mission planning, coordination, and training workflows.

 - Validate that our tools hold up in practice: build reference multi-agent UAV autonomy on top of the product, exercise the full workflow from simulation through deployment on real airframes, and turn what breaks into product requirements.

 - Define how simulation should be used across the development cycle, including where fidelity matters, how tuning and validation workflows should be structured, and what it takes to close the gap between simulated and real flight behavior.

 - Collaborate frequently with US-based product and engineering teams to deliver features on shared roadmaps, operating as the Korea-based extension of the global product teams.

 - Contribute to system-level design and architecture, ensuring scalability, reliability, and performance.

 - Run technical deep dives with Korean defense customers on selected features, probing their operational requirements, clarifying ambiguous needs, and translating what you learn into product specifications and roadmap input.

 - Guide customers on how to get the most out of our tools when developing their own multi-agent unmanned systems, drawing on your own hands-on experience.

 - Mentor engineers and share domain knowledge across the Korea team.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field.

 - 5+ years of professional engineering experience, or equivalent research experience, in a fast-paced, customer-oriented environment.

 - Hands-on experience in at least one of the following two areas:
   
   - Unmanned aerial systems development: You have built and flown real unmanned aircraft, and understand UAS development end to end. You know what tuning process an airframe has to go through before it flies reliably, and where simulation does and does not help along the way.
   
   - Multi-agent optimization and control: You have researched or engineered algorithms that coordinate multiple agents to carry out a mission optimally, including the use of ML methods such as reinforcement learning for this purpose.

 - Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, C++, or similar.

 - Experience working on complex, multidisciplinary projects in a collaborative team setting.

 - Strong problem-solving skills and ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

 - Excellent English communication skills, both written and verbal, for effective daily collaboration with the USA team and documentation.

 - Ability to lead technical discussions directly with customers, drawing out requirements, challenging assumptions, and explaining design trade-offs to both engineers and domain experts.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience across both of the areas listed above.

 - Familiarity with flight control stacks and autopilot software (e.g., PX4, ArduPilot), and with the ground control and data link elements of a complete unmanned aerial system.

 - Familiarity with ATR, drone swarming, path planning, or aerospace control systems as a domain user perspective informing tool design.

 - Experience building simulation platforms, ML training infrastructure, or developer tooling for robotics, autonomy, or defense applications.

 - Experience in closed-network / air-gapped deployment environments common in defense.

 - Professional fluency in Korean, for direct technical engagement with Korean defense customers.


WHY JOIN US?

 - Build the products that the Korean and global defense ecosystem relies on for autonomy development.

 - Be part of a collaborative, customer-focused team that values innovation and rapid delivery.

 - Opportunity to lead, mentor, and make a significant impact in a high-growth, mission-driven organization.

 - Join our vibrant team in Korea, working on-site, collaborating daily with our USA team, and engaging with customers to drive innovation in unmanned vehicle autonomy.

As a new team focused on platformization, we offer a rare opportunity to own core work leveraged across the entire organization.

HD maps go stale the moment they're built — lanes get repainted, stop lines move, roads close. You'll own the live map on Applied's onboard stack: a real-time fused estimate of the world built from map priors and live perception, from the estimation core to the change-detection and trust semantics the planner consumes, across every vehicle vertical we serve. This layer is early and has no incumbent design. You'll set the architecture and define the interfaces rather than tune inside someone else's system. We encourage engineers to take ownership of technical and product decisions and to interact closely with users to collect feedback.

 


AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Own the onboard live-map estimator end to end: fuse HD map priors with live perception into a single, real-time estimate of the world the rest of the stack can trust

 - Build our onboard map change detection: classify situations like boundary shifts, stop-line moves, and road closures from the divergence between map and perception, and define when the planner should stop trusting the map

 - Define the map trust contracts the planner builds against: confidence semantics, degraded-mode behavior, and the operating points that hold across vehicle programs

 - Build the evaluation backbone, ground-truth and metrics pipelines, operating points, and regression testing that keep estimator and detector quality from silently drifting

 - Ship estimation code in modern C++ that meets real-time budgets on embedded compute

 - Extend the loop offboard over time: aggregate divergence detections across fleet drive logs into map freshness and correction pipelines

 


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent

 - 5+ years building production software, including at least one shipped system where they owned the estimation core

 - State estimation fundamentals proven in production: factor graphs and/or filtering, data association, uncertainty representation and propagation, and 3D geometry and transforms

 - Experience fusing heterogeneous sources such as prior map data, perception output, and raw sensors, into a single world estimate, with rigorous error characterization

 - Strong modern C++ and the ability to make estimation code meet real-time budgets on embedded compute

 - Rigorous evaluation practice: has built ground-truth or metrics pipelines and used them to hold a shipped operating point and prevent regressions

 - Judgment about uncertainty: understands the difference between an error that degrades gracefully and one that is catastrophic, and designs the system accordingly

 - Experience defining a system and its interfaces and negotiating those contracts with consumer teams

 


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Map change detection or live/lifelong mapping experience

 - HD map semantics: lane graphs, topology, map formats and their failure modes

 - GTSAM or comparable factor-graph frameworks; Lie group methods

 - Degraded-mode or integrity-monitor design for a safety-relevant function

 - MS/PhD with a focus on state estimation or SLAM

ABOUT THE ROLE

Our Localization, Calibration, and Mapping team delivers high-integrity solutions that let autonomous systems navigate with precision in real-time, safety-critical environments — across consumer automotive, trucking, mining, and construction. As a new team focused on platformization, we offer a rare opportunity to own core work leveraged across the entire organization.

HD maps go stale the moment they're built — lanes get repainted, stop lines move, roads close. You'll own the live map on Applied's onboard stack: a real-time fused estimate of the world built from map priors and live perception, from the estimation core to the change-detection and trust semantics the planner consumes, across every vehicle vertical we serve. This layer is early and has no incumbent design. You'll set the architecture and define the interfaces rather than tune inside someone else's system. We encourage engineers to take ownership of technical and product decisions and to interact closely with users to collect feedback.

 


AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Own the onboard live-map estimator end to end: fuse HD map priors with live perception into a single, real-time estimate of the world the rest of the stack can trust

 - Build our onboard map change detection: classify situations like boundary shifts, stop-line moves, and road closures from the divergence between map and perception, and define when the planner should stop trusting the map

 - Define the map trust contracts the planner builds against: confidence semantics, degraded-mode behavior, and the operating points that hold across vehicle programs

 - Build the evaluation backbone, ground-truth and metrics pipelines, operating points, and regression testing that keep estimator and detector quality from silently drifting

 - Ship estimation code in modern C++ that meets real-time budgets on embedded compute

 - Extend the loop offboard over time: aggregate divergence detections across fleet drive logs into map freshness and correction pipelines

 


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent

 - 5+ years of experience building production software, including at least one shipped system where they owned the estimation core

 - State estimation fundamentals proven in production: factor graphs and/or filtering, data association, uncertainty representation and propagation, and 3D geometry and transforms

 - Experience fusing heterogeneous sources such as prior map data, perception output, and raw sensors, into a single world estimate, with rigorous error characterization

 - Strong modern C++ and the ability to make estimation code meet real-time budgets on embedded compute

 - Rigorous evaluation practice: has built ground-truth or metrics pipelines and used them to hold a shipped operating point and prevent regressions

 - Judgment about uncertainty: understands the difference between an error that degrades gracefully and one that is catastrophic, and designs the system accordingly

 - Experience defining a system and its interfaces and negotiating those contracts with consumer teams

 


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Map change detection or live/lifelong mapping experience

 - HD map semantics: lane graphs, topology, map formats and their failure modes

 - GTSAM or comparable factor-graph frameworks; Lie group methods

 - Degraded-mode or integrity-monitor design for a safety-relevant function

 - MS/PhD with a focus on state estimation or SLAM

You will architect, build, test, and break hardware, then use what you learn to make it tougher. You'll work in the field as much as at the bench, and your decisions will define how Applied's hardware performs on real machines in dust, vibration, heat, mud, and shock.

 - Interface with industrial customers as a representative of the hardware organization

 - Be hands-on: prototype, build, install, debug, and test hardware on real machines, not just review designs

 - Define and drive survivability: determine how sensors, compute, harnesses, connectors, and enclosures will hold up to vibration, shock, dust, water ingress, thermal extremes, EMI, and years of heavy use

 - Design and run environmental and durability testing, analyze failures, and drive root cause and design fixes

 - Lead integration of sensors (lidar, radar, cameras, GNSS/IMU), compute, power, networking, and actuation onto OEM heavy equipment

 - Understand the host machine (powertrain, electrohydraulics, vehicle electrical architecture, CAN/J1939) well enough to integrate safely and reliably

 - Be the technical authority and escalation point for hardware tradeoffs across mechanical, electrical, software, and test

 - Lead hardware design reviews, set engineering standards, and mentor other engineers

 - Support field deployments and commissioning at mine sites, farms, and customer facilities

We're looking for someone who has:

 - BS/MS in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, or a related field

 - 10+ years of hands-on hardware engineering experience on heavy industrial or off-highway vehicles (mining, agriculture, construction, or similar)

 - Strong command of the whole hardware system: mechanical design, electrical architecture, power distribution, harness design, and how they interact

 - A track record of designing hardware to survive harsh environments, with real experience in vibration, shock, ingress protection, thermal management, and EMI

 - Hands-on experience in the lab and in the field: building prototypes, wiring and debugging systems, running tests, and diagnosing failures on real machines

 - Deep knowledge of how industrial machines work, including powertrains, hydraulics, braking, steering, and CAN/J1939 networks

 - Experience integrating hardware onto OEM or retrofit equipment

 - Familiarity with autonomy hardware such as lidar, radar, cameras, GNSS/IMU, and ruggedized compute

 - Systems-level thinking and the ability to make architecture decisions and defend them

 - Experience with reliability and qualification testing (environmental testing, HALT, field durability)

 - Comfort working directly with OEMs, customers, and site operators, including extended time at mine sites and farms

 - Experience with functional safety or machine safety standards (ISO 25119, ISO 13849, ISO 17757, ISO 26262)

 - Experience with autonomous haulage, precision agriculture, or other autonomous industrial systems

Data Engine powers the data workflows behind Applied Intuition's autonomy programs across Cars, Trucks, Industrials, and Defense. We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to make it a coherent platform that technical teams can discover, adopt, and rely on—from bringing data into the system to producing useful, traceable datasets.

Your first customers are the engineers and researchers building autonomy inside Applied. You will work directly with them to understand how they get work done, identify where shared capabilities can replace duplicated effort, and turn their needs into a clear product strategy. Your responsibility extends across ingestion, processing, data discovery, enrichment, quality, and dataset delivery—not just the boundaries of a single engineering team.

You will also own the external product roadmap, customer discovery, and packaging for this platform, working with commercial partners on pricing and go-to-market. You will determine what transfers to external customers and what additional deployment, onboarding, and support capabilities they need.

Success is helping teams complete important workflows more easily, reuse capabilities across programs, and depend less on bespoke integrations and engineering assistance.

At Applied Intuition, you will

 - Own the end-to-end product. Set the vision, roadmap, and priorities across multiple teams behind our Data Engine. Define the workflows we support, their users, and what a reliable production experience requires.

 - Stay close to users. Observe real workflows, interview users and non-users, investigate workarounds, and combine that evidence with usage and support signals. Make sure teams understand what happened to their feedback and why.

 - Build shared capabilities without erasing real differences. Decide what belongs in the common platform, what needs configuration or extension points, and what should remain program-specific. Make explicit choices about what not to build.

 - Own adoption beyond launch. Partner with design and engineering on APIs, interfaces, documentation, examples, onboarding, and migrations. Help users find existing capabilities and retire duplicated implementations when the shared path is ready.

 - Make technical tradeoffs with engineering. Translate user needs into clear requirements and acceptance criteria. Balance reliability, data quality, latency, cost, compatibility, and delivery speed while respecting security and data-residency constraints.

 - Connect internal and external needs. Lead external discovery, define a repeatable offering and its limits, and build a commercial roadmap with sales and customer-facing partners. Avoid turning individual customer requests into permanent product forks.

 - Measure outcomes and communicate decisions. Track workflow success, onboarding time, adoption, support effort, and reuse. Explain priorities, tradeoffs, and risks clearly to program teams and leadership.

We're looking for someone who has

 - MS/BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience

 - 4+ years of Product Management experience at a top tech company or high-growth startup

 - A record of owning complex technical products from discovery through delivery, adoption, and iteration, with senior-level responsibility for decisions and results.

 - Experience serving technical users through a shared platform, developer product, or data/ML product, including reconciling competing needs across multiple teams or customers.

 - Strong discovery skills: you can distinguish a requested feature from the underlying problem and show how user evidence changed a product decision.

 - Sound platform judgment: you can balance reuse with necessary specialization, set support boundaries, and sequence migration without blocking users' work.

 - Technical fluency in data flows, APIs, workflow orchestration, data quality, and production operations. You can discuss architectural tradeoffs with engineers.



Nice to have

 - Experience with autonomy, robotics, sensor data, or other physical AI workflows.

 - Experience with ingestion, catalogs and lineage, data processing, ML data pipelines, or workflow orchestration.

 - Experience converting an internal platform into an external product, or supporting customer-controlled and multi-region deployments.

 - Prior software engineering experience or hands-on work with technical users, APIs, and developer tooling.

This is a builder role, not an administrator role. You will turn work that runs on tribal knowledge and one-off fixes into documented, measured, repeatable programs with clear owners and controls.

You will be helping define the center of excellence model on the People team: the escalation point for employee matters, a data connoisseur that owns data fidelity , and the person who decides where work should live as the team matures from reactive support to a proactive shared-services model. You will lead cross-functional projects and use AI to shape the employee experience.

 


AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Define the People Ops operating model: what is standardized and centralized, what stays with People Partners or other COEs, and how work transitions with continuity and measurement built in

 - Assess the maturity of each core People process (onboarding, offboarding, job changes, comp cycles, leaves, time off, rotations) and run a roadmap to move each from ad hoc to documented, measured, and automated

 - Be the operational partner to People Business Partners: execute reorgs, promotions, performance actions, and exits they drive; supply the data and process support behind their work

 - Set standards for process design, documentation, SLAs, and handoffs; own the SOP library and knowledge base so answers live in a system

 - Support the build of audit-ready controls (recurring data audits, approval trails, segregation of duties) for SOX

 - Define service-quality metrics (ticket volume, resolution time, error rate, employee satisfaction) and use them to decide what to fix next

 - Run proactive audits across Workday and connected systems to catch errors before they reach payroll, equity, or board reporting

 - Serve as a functional Workday owner: business process design from requirements through configuration, testing, and post-launch iteration

 - Use AI and low-code tools to prototype and ship People Ops automations; know when a gap needs a lightweight internal tool versus a technical build with IT or Systems

 - Resolve the hardest cases in benefits, leaves, time off, rotations, and sensitive org changes with precision, empathy, and clear written communication

 - Partner with Finance, Legal, IT, Recruiting, and Payroll on projects that mature processes and policies for the business

 - Lead change management for process redesigns and new tools: communication, training, adoption tracking, and feedback loops

 - Identify gaps in our operational cadence before they're pointed out to you, and drive the fixes

 - Bachelor's Degree and 5+ years of practical experience experience in a People or HR-related role

 - Hands-on use of AI and low-code tools (Claude, Lovable, Zapier, Apps Script, SQL) to build People Ops automations or lightweight internal tools

 - Experience with Carta, Ashby, and Jira help desk, or comparable equity, ATS, and ticketing systems

 - Experience partnering with IT or HRIS teams on integrations and translating business needs into requirements and test plans

 - Background in Lean, Six Sigma, or service design applied to HR processes

 - Experience supporting compliance audits (SOX, EEO-1, benefits-plan) and immigration programs


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience in high-growth technology companies, particularly automotive or autonomous vehicle industries

 - Direct experience scaling People Ops functions from early-stage to larger organizational structures

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Perception Engineer, you will help build the perception layer of an autonomy stack for uncrewed air vehicles. The team turns noisy, intermittent data from many sensors and teammates into a reliable picture of the airspace. 

This role spans classical state estimation and tracking, sensor fusion, and learning-based prediction. Increasingly, those models adapt online during an engagement from limited and delayed feedback. The engineer will design and implement real-time C++ algorithms, build the tooling and simulation studies that show whether they work, and carry ideas from research prototypes into deployable software. We need someone fluent in both estimation theory and machine learning, rigorous about measuring results, and comfortable working at the line between research and production.

 


AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Develop, integrate, and adapt cutting-edge AI/ML algorithms running on the perception autonomy stack to collect relevant information across a suite of platform sensors

 - Create interfacing software to autonomously control sensors (e.g., EO, IR, acoustics, radar, and RF)

 - Collaborate across the sensor, tracking, and autonomy teams to ensure seamless deployment of heterogeneous platform swarms in on-site DoD testing and demonstration events

 - Deploy containerized solutions to embedded Linux devices, leveraging computer-in-the-loop testing and profiling, and efficiently collecting performance data

 - Interact with the DoD customer to understand their use cases, requirements, and triage needs during field events to deliver a superior customer experience
   


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - BS/MS in Electrical, Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field, plus 3+ years building perception or estimation software for autonomous systems.

 - Strong modern C++ (17/20) for real-time, performance-critical code on Linux. Comfortable with linear algebra libraries (e.g. Eigen) and profiling.

 - Solid grounding in state estimation: Kalman filter variants (EKF/UKF), multiple-model filters (IMM), and covariance and uncertainty handling.

 - Experience with multi-target tracking and sensor fusion: data association, track management, and fusing heterogeneous sensors that report intermittently and with noise.

 - Working knowledge of machine learning for prediction, including sequence models (RNN/LSTM, transformers), training pipelines, and evaluating models on held-out data.

 - Python for data pipelines, analysis and visualization of logged and simulated runs.

 - Experience validating algorithms in simulation and with recorded data: designing experiments, defining metrics, and reading results honestly.

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Vision, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field2+ years of experience in industry.

Security Requirements:

 - Must be a U.S. Citizen

 - Must hold or be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance

For more information about U.S. security clearances: click here https://www.state.gov/securityclearances.



NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience with online, real-time learning: models that adapt during operation, not just offline training.

 - Background in adaptive control or learning-based estimation (e.g. concurrent learning, Lyapunov-based learning, Bayesian or recursive least-squares parameter estimation).

 - Experience learning from intermittent, delayed or sparse feedback, where ground truth arrives late or only sometimes.

 - Behavior and intent prediction for other agents, including models of non-cooperative or adversarial actors.

 - Deploying small neural networks in C++ without heavy ML frameworks, under tight latency and compute budgets.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Applied Intuition's Digital Proving Grounds (DPGs) give the Department of War a vendor-neutral place to test autonomous systems from many companies together, against a real mission, before they reach the field. A DPG covers the full path from software-in-the-loop (SIL) simulation to hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), live-virtual-constructive (LVC), and live exercises. Teams find integration problems in simulation, where fixes take hours, instead of at a live event, where they take weeks.

DPGs run on Axion, Applied's defense toolchain, with Axion Sim at the core. Applied ran VREX for the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, a DPG that put air, surface, and undersea vehicles from different vendors on one mission. CDAO then selected Applied to build the platform for Autonomy Factory, which brings this approach to programs across the Department of War on autonomy.mil http://autonomy.mil.

The technology works in programs. The next step is a product that program offices, test organizations, and mission engineers choose, adopt, and come back to, without Applied engineers supporting events. As the Product Manager for Digital Proving Grounds, you will own the product strategy, roadmap, and requirements for DPGs and Axion Sim. This is an individual-contributor role. You will work as the product peer to the engineering lead for Axion Sim and drive outcomes through influence across engineering, design, business development, and delivery.


AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL

 - Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for DPGs and Axion Sim. Decide what becomes repeatable product and what stays program-specific work.

 - Find product-market fit. Run discovery with program offices, test and evaluation organizations, mission engineers, and autonomy vendors. Learn who buys, what they need to prove, and what brings them back for the next event. Work with business development and capture to turn what you learn into offers that win programs.

 - Define the sim-to-live workflow. Shape how a team goes from a mission and its concept of operations to test scenarios, then to SIL at scale, HIL rig checkout, LVC, and live events, with results that carry across each stage.

Your work will run on real trucks on public roads, and it will be measured by how far the fleet drives between failures.

 - Shape how Level 4 autonomy and physical AI reach the real world, with software that runs on vehicles on public roads.

 - Design the runtime architecture of the onboard stack: how processes are scheduled, how they communicate, and how the system degrades when a component fails.

 - Combine state-of-the-art AI and classical modules to meet the high performance and high reliability requirements

 - Trace on-road failures from an application symptom to its root cause in the kernel, the hardware, or the middleware, and fix it.

 - Make a real-time system faster and more predictable on production compute, and prove it with measurements.

 - Decide how the platform detects and escalates faults, up to commanding the truck to pull over safely.

 - Build the measurement systems that tell the whole program whether the stack is getting faster and more reliable.

 - Bring the Applied Intuition self-driving stack up on new compute platforms and new vehicles.

 - Work alongside some of the strongest engineers in autonomy across perception, planning, controls, hardware, and safety, and set broad, cross-functional technical direction with them.
   
   


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - Bachelor's in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field.

 - 4+ years of experience shipping complex software in C++14 and above.

 - Strong system design and engineering fundamentals.

 - Experience leading the design of a system, from design document through production.

 - Working knowledge of operating system internals, such as scheduling, memory management, threading, and inter-process communication.

 - Experience debugging problems that cross the boundary between application code, the operating system, and hardware.
   
   


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience developing onboard application software, in autonomy, ADAS, or robotics.

 - Experience with real-time systems, an RTOS, or QNX.

 - Experience with robotics middleware or shared-memory communication, such as ROS 2 or DDS.

 - Experience with profiling and tracing tools.

 - Experience with vehicle hardware and networks such as CAN.
